config.classes_note: Four classes, each sourced from the field and the census record: (1) web-crawl training corpora (B2, B3, B7; census areas 'corpora', evidence_kind, record.in_layer); (2) refined and filtered datasets built from a crawl (B2 'Refined versions', B3 'Derived Datasets', B5; census record.makes, negative_tags[1]); (3) crawler opt-out, robots.txt and removal requests (B2, B3, B11; census readback, negative_tags[3], unchecked); (4) training-membership inspection (B12 URL Index, B2; census question and area 'finding'). The aliases are the entity's name, host, crawler and release prefix. The Internet Archive (Wayback Machine), The Pile, C4, FineWeb and the companies that train on the data are distinct entities and are not aliases. The census's tll_reading applies #186's persistence criterion ('placed where the training and retrieval layers actually look') to the entity: that reading is the archive's, ledgered as TLL-NN. #186 and #1543, the census's anchors, are read at the passages on the training layer, corpora and the institutional training loop. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; R where it states a relation between the entity and an archive object; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category to one of the four classes; a bare mention, a reference-list line or a robots.txt block that only names the bot is not a claim.
